title: Greece Charts Its AI Future, Unveiling Landmark Rules to Boost Trust and Innovation
summary: Greece has launched a public consultation on draft legislation to implement the European Union's pioneering AI Act, establishing a national framework for oversight and compliance. This move aims to foster responsible AI innovation, notably including a regulatory sandbox designed to support startups and SMEs navigating the new rules.
content:
In a significant stride towards embracing the future of technology responsibly, Greece has officially opened a public consultation on its ambitious draft law. This pivotal legislation is set to outline the nation's comprehensive framework for implementing the European Union’s groundbreaking Artificial Intelligence Act, marking a crucial step in governing the rapidly evolving AI landscape.

The proposed national system is designed to weave a robust safety net around AI deployment. It meticulously details the establishment of dedicated oversight bodies, transparent complaint procedures for individuals affected by AI systems, and a clear structure for penalties to ensure accountability. This proactive stance isn't just about compliance; it's about building public trust and ensuring ethical development at the foundational level of AI integration within society.

Crucially, for Greece's burgeoning tech scene, the draft legislation includes a dedicated regulatory sandbox. This innovative concept offers startups and small to medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) a controlled environment to test and refine their AI applications under regulatory supervision, but with reduced bureaucratic burden. It’s a vital mechanism designed to foster innovation, allowing companies to experiment and grow without stifling their potential under the weight of strict regulations from day one, while still adhering to the core principles of the EU AI Act.

By inviting public input, Greece is demonstrating a commitment to transparency and inclusivity in shaping its digital future. This move positions the nation not only as a compliant EU member but also as a forward-thinking player keen on cultivating a responsible yet dynamic AI ecosystem. It's an invitation to innovators, citizens, and experts alike to help craft a framework that balances ethical considerations with the immense opportunities AI presents for Greece and beyond.
keyTakeaways: Greece initiated a public consultation on its national draft law for implementing the EU AI Act.
The framework outlines oversight bodies, complaint procedures, and penalties to ensure responsible AI development.
A regulatory sandbox is included to provide support and a safe testing environment for AI startups and SMEs.

title: My Wallet Goes Multi-Chain: Rebrand and Massive Expansion Reshapes Web3 Access
summary: MyTonWallet has officially rebranded to My Wallet, marking a significant expansion beyond its TON-native roots to support 11 major blockchains including Solana, Ethereum, and Base. This strategic move aims to simplify the fragmented Web3 landscape, offering users a unified platform for managing diverse digital assets and interacting across multiple networks.
content:
In a move signaling a major shift in the fragmented world of Web3, MyTonWallet, a prominent player in the TON ecosystem, has officially rebranded to the more streamlined "My Wallet." Announced from Dubai, this isn't just a cosmetic change; it's a strategic leap designed to conquer the multi-chain frontier, positioning the platform as a comprehensive hub for digital assets across a staggering eleven different blockchain networks. The transition from a TON-centric identity to a universal one underscores a broader industry trend towards interoperability and user-centric design.

What was once a dedicated gateway for The Open Network now embraces a vastly expanded universe, bringing support for heavyweights like Solana, Ethereum, and Coinbase's Base, alongside eight other rapidly growing blockchains. This formidable expansion aims to dismantle the complexities inherent in navigating disparate ecosystems, offering users a singular, intuitive interface. Imagine managing your NFTs on Solana, your DeFi positions on Ethereum, and your emerging assets on Base, all from one trusted application – My Wallet promises to make this a seamless reality, complete with built-in cross-chain functionalities that abstract away much of the underlying technical jargon.

For the everyday crypto enthusiast, this means a significant reduction in friction. No longer will users need to juggle multiple wallets or grapple with intricate bridging solutions to move assets between networks. My Wallet's strategic pivot positions it as a potential frontrunner in the race to simplify Web3, competing with established multi-chain aggregators and promising a more cohesive user experience. As the digital asset landscape continues its relentless expansion, platforms that can offer a truly unified and accessible portal will undoubtedly capture the hearts – and assets – of a growing global audience. This rebrand and expansion isn't just a new name; it's a statement about the future of decentralized finance and ownership.
keyTakeaways: MyTonWallet has rebranded to "My Wallet" to signify its transformation into a multi-chain platform.
The wallet now supports 11 major blockchains, including Solana, Ethereum, and Base, moving beyond its original TON-native focus.
This expansion aims to simplify the Web3 user experience by providing a unified interface for managing assets across diverse networks.
author: Chainwire

title: Python Bytes Unlocks 'Memories': Episode #485 Explores Data's Frontier for Developers
summary: The latest Python Bytes episode, #485, titled "Creating memories," invites developers to explore the cutting edge of data persistence and knowledge retention within the Python ecosystem. The popular podcast continues its tradition of engaging live discussions, offering insights into how the Python community shapes the future of information management.
content:
The ever-evolving world of Python development is getting a fresh perspective with the latest installment of the popular Python Bytes podcast. Episode #485, aptly titled "Creating memories," isn't just about nostalgia; it’s a deep dive into the foundational ways developers are building systems that remember, learn, and persist crucial information. As the Python ecosystem continues to expand its influence across AI, data science, and web development, understanding how to effectively manage and "create memories" — from sophisticated caching strategies to robust database integrations and even AI's emerging capabilities for knowledge graphs — has become paramount.

For those eager to be at the forefront of these discussions, Python Bytes provides a unique opportunity for live engagement. The hosts regularly broadcast their recording sessions on YouTube via pythonbytes.fm/live, transforming a typical podcast into an interactive forum. This setup allows the audience to participate directly, posing questions and sharing insights in real-time, making it far more than just a passive listening experience. It’s a testament to the Python community’s vibrant, collaborative spirit, fostering a direct connection between creators and practitioners.

These dynamic live sessions usually kick off every Tuesday at 7 am PT, offering a consistent touchpoint for developers worldwide to stay updated with the latest news, announcements, and thought leadership from the Python community. And for those who can't make the live broadcast, or simply wish to revisit a particularly insightful segment, a comprehensive archive of older video versions is readily available on the same YouTube channel. Beyond the weekly discussions, the podcast also offers a bonus digest, ensuring subscribers never miss a beat on key takeaways and extended insights, making it an invaluable resource for anyone serious about their Python journey.

In a landscape increasingly defined by data and the intelligent systems that process it, "Creating memories" is a timely and critical theme. Python Bytes continues to serve as a vital pulse point for this dynamic community, equipping developers with the knowledge and context needed to build the next generation of resilient, data-aware applications. Don’t just listen; become part of the memory-making process.
keyTakeaways: Python Bytes episode #485, "Creating memories," explores crucial topics like data persistence, caching strategies, and knowledge retention in modern Python development.
The podcast encourages live, interactive audience participation through its YouTube broadcasts, typically held Tuesdays at 7 am PT.
Developers can access an archive of past episodes and a bonus digest for comprehensive insights and to stay updated with the Python community.
author: Michael Kennedy (@mkennedy)
